title: Nested array mixed with a scalar - the documented output does not exist
rationale: This exact document appears in the MapFlattener class javadoc, which claims the output is {data_name, data_value}. HALF of that claim is still false and half was repaired in 2.1.0. Still false: the sentinel maps to the base key "data", not "data_value". No longer false: the javadoc's padding IS now implemented, though not in the shape it described - data_name=[["A"],null] and data=[[null],"text"], one slot per outer position, with an inner list of nulls where a nested position lacked the column and a bare null only where the position held no nested list at all. A fixture whose value is that it contradicts the shipped documentation, now on one axis rather than two.
catchesBugClass: The leaf-versus-branch key collision in setNestedValue, where a one-segment key silently clobbers a subtree built from a longer key sharing its name - here "data" destroys "data_name". It NO LONGER catches "documentation that describes a padding control that was never implemented" : the control exists as of 2.1.0 (BL-018), and that half of this row is recorded as closed rather than left implied.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the reverse collision order (subtree written after the leaf), which takes the _value-wrapper branch and fails differently. It also cannot tell whether the javadoc or the code is the intended behaviour for the SENTINEL KEY; a human must classify that, and the fix must not be to edit the javadoc to match the code. It does not measure the positional contract in isolation either - MapFlattenerNestedArrayAlignmentTest owns that, and its two strings for this document must stay identical to the ones recorded here.

predicted.detail: Actual flatten output uses the base key "data" rather than the documented data_value. The positional half of this row was repaired in 2.1.0: the columns are now padded to the outer element count, so data_name=[["A"],null] describes outer position 0 and data=[[null],"text"] describes outer position 1. What remains DEFECT is the sentinel key itself plus the setNestedValue leaf-versus-branch collision on reconstruct, which drops data_name entirely and returns data alone.
